oral-bioavailability outcome.

condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

The lowest reported values in the visible contexts (papaverine 22%, AZD0837 22%) still meet the F>=20% threshold, so none of the records provides affirmative evidence for F<20%.
Fasted-state and food-insensitive oral bioavailability data (vernakalant 58–71% in fasted volunteers; apixaban ~50% unaffected by food) support the fasted query condition.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral-versus-intravenous PK measurement is available for the query molecule itself.
No visible context shares the exact quinuclidine-quinoline scaffold, so transfer is based on general small-molecule oral PK behavior rather than a close structural match.
The query is strongly ionized at physiological pH (neutral fraction 0.01, basic pKa 9.28), which may reduce passive permeability; no matched absorption data are available to resolve this uncertainty.
Some supporting records are qualitative or model-derived (e.g., CPI-0610 'good' bioavailability; ONO-4641 predicted F), adding uncertainty to the transfer.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F>=20%) because the physicochemical prior is favorable and all visible human oral-bioavailability records are at or above the 20% threshold, with no affirmative evidence for F<20%. Confidence is moderate because the exact scaffold is not represented in the visible contexts and strong basic ionization introduces permeability uncertainty.
